newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sees strong R&D, private sector leads.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sees strong R&D, private sector leads.

text.p: Research and development in Singapore was robust last year with the private sector leading in expenditure, the National Science & Technology Board (NSTB) said in a statement on Monday.
The latest survey showed gross expenditure on research and development (GERD) was Singapore $1,367 million (US$976 million), up 16.3 percent over the previous year.
This represents 1.13 percent of gross domestic product.
Expenditure grew at a significant rate over the last five years from $571.1 million, it said.
The private sector continued to lead in research and development, making up for 64.5 percent of gross expenditure, the NSTB said.
"The overall picture which has emerged from the 1995 R&D survey shows clearly the response to the need to rapidly move up the technological ladder," said Teo Ming Kian, chairman of NSTB.
The electronics sector remains the leading industry group in spending on R&D. It hit $430.7 million, nearly half of private sector GERD with an increase of $72.1 million over 1994.
The electrical industry follows at $72.14 million, the chemical industry at $65 million and machinery industry at $56.98 million.
The survey, conducted from May to September, has been carried out annually by the NSTB since 1991. It measures the intensity and scope of R&D activities in Singapore.
